mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 8.0% indicates severe labor market distress that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 8.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal robust consumer demand that drives corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO) during late-cycle economic slowdowns signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO declines, or Rank IC for INDPRO in late-cycle regime falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS has increased over the prior 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% triggers expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates broad-based economic strength that accelerates corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint signal of rising GDPC1 and HOUST fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate during monetary tightening cycles increases borrowing costs that depress corporate investment and consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is rising, or Rank IC for tightening cycle falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.
